title: Transient tenant egress cross-talk during peering rekey causing DNS resolver leakage
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent delivery of DNS responses that included private tenant hostnames or responses sourced from the wrong resolver during VPC peering rekey windows and peering-control-plane upgrades. Symptoms were transient (10s-2m), but correlated with peering tunnel rekey and route-flap events. This caused customer-visible host resolution anomalies and triggered escalations from two customers running strict isolation workloads (one healthcare, one financial).

What happened (high level):
- During scheduled and rolling peering rekey events the control-plane briefly updated dataplane route state and tunnel keys.
- A small fraction of in-flight egress flows were reassigned to a different SNAT mapping because ephemeral SNAT port affinity was rebalanced while conntrack entries remained present.
- Asymmetric egress (request goes out via path A, response arrives back on path B) plus stale resolver affinity allowed cached external resolver replies to be returned to the wrong tenant interface in edge cases. That in turn led to private-hostname leakage or incorrect resolution for the requesting tenant.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by tracing + packet captures):
- Peering rekey triggers a race between: peering-route programming + NAT table reallocation + conntrack cleanup. We observed conntrack entries being retained while the L3 path index used for per-tenant SNAT mapping changed.
- Our SNAT allocator does not pin port ranges to a tenant while a route-change is mid-transaction, allowing two tenants to temporarily share the same ephemeral mapping before full cleanup.
- DNS caching on the edge filer was too eager to use resolver associations based on source IP without verifying the current tenant binding (TTL reuse across affinity swaps).

Reproduction notes:
- Deterministic repro when running repeated IKE rekeys (simulated peering rekey in staging) while running high-volume small UDP/53 flows from multiple tenants simultaneously.
- Packet captures (pcap) attached show responses for tenant B arriving with the source IP/port that had been recently used by tenant A. conntrack queries show orphaned entries for the previous mapping.

Immediate mitigations applied (hotfixes rolled in prod):
- Short-term: Introduced a 30s guard window after peering rekey where we refuse to reuse recently freed SNAT ephemeral port ranges across different tenant namespaces (mitigates cross-tenant reuse). Rolled to 3 regions as an emergency config change.
- Short-term: Edge DNS resolver now validates tenant binding on cached DNS results during the guard window; if mismatch detected, it forces a fresh external resolution.
- Notified affected customers and applied temporary traffic pinning for their dedicated pools while we fully remediate.

Planned long-term fixes (RFC + PRs):
- Implement conntrack namespace isolation per tenant so that conntrack entries cannot be observed/used across tenant contexts even during route/key churn (design doc in Confluence: /r/peering/conntrack-tenant-iso).
- Rework SNAT allocator to provide conservative port-range affinity guarantees during peering topology changes and to coordinate with the route programming pipeline.
- Add synchronous conntrack prune step as part of a controlled peering key flip when safe to do so, with rate-limited prune to prevent CPU spikes.
- Improve telemetry: add a peering-rekey->snat-affinity drift metric and a DNS-cache-mismatch counter that surfaces to the Console with customer-scoped alerts.

Customer communications and impact:
- Customers impacted: "CedarHealth" (healthcare) and "LedgerOne" (financial). Both opened P1 escalations. CedarHealth reported policy violations risk due to private hostname leakage. LedgerOne observed intermittent routing failures impacting request success rates (~0.6% of queries during incidents).
- Legal/Trust: Briefed account leads and Security for required disclosure. No stored PII was exposed; this was DNS/egress-resolution leakage only.

Artifacts and references:
- Relevant packet captures: s3://redwood-prod-artifacts/peering-rekey/pcap-2025-01-24-cedar.pcap (redacted)
- Staging repro harness: github.com/redwood/infra-peering-repro branch: peering-rekey-stress
- Emergency config PR: github.com/redwood/platform-config/pull/4215 (rolled 2025-01-30)
- Follow-up design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PEERING/Conntrack+Tenant+Isolation

Open questions and trade-offs:
- Aggressive conntrack pruning reduces cross-tenant risk but may temporarily drop long-lived flows for latency-sensitive customers; we need canarying and opt-in exceptions.
- Port-range affinity windows increase SNAT exhaustion risk under heavy multi-tenant churn; we may need to increase ephemeral pool sizes or implement per-tenant pools for large customers.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- No cross-tenant DNS resolution anomalies observed in canary after new conntrack isolation (2 weeks, <0.01% repro),
- New peering rekey metrics exist and alert when drift exceeds threshold,
- Postmortem published with customer follow-up completed and RCA approved by Security & PM.
